अंक 1: भविष्यवाणी और षड्यंत्र

कहानी की शुरुआत तीन चुड़ैलों से होती है जो तूफान और बिजली के बीच मिलती हैं। वे युद्ध के बाद मैकबेथ से मिलने की योजना बनाती हैं और अपने प्रसिद्ध वाक्य "जो सुंदर है वह भयानक है, और जो भयानक है वह सुंदर है" के साथ नाटक का अशुभ वातावरण स्थापित करती हैं।

राजा डंकन को युद्ध की खबरें मिलती हैं। एक घायल कप्तान मैकबेथ की असाधारण बहादुरी का वर्णन करता है - कैसे उसने विद्रोही मैकडोनवाल्ड को "नाभि से ठुड्डी तक" चीर दिया। डंकन प्रसन्न होकर मैकबेथ को "वीर चचेरे भाई, योग्य सज्जन" कहते हैं। जब खबर आती है कि कॉडर का थेन गद्दार निकला है, तो डंकन उसे मृत्युदंड देते हैं और मैकबेथ को उसकी उपाधि प्रदान करते हैं।

युद्ध से लौटते समय, मैकबेथ और बैंको चुड़ैलों से मिलते हैं। चुड़ैलें भविष्यवाणी करती हैं कि मैकबेथ ग्लैमिस का थेन, कॉडर का थेन, और भविष्य में राजा बनेगा। बैंको को विरोधाभासी भविष्यवाणी मिलती है - वह मैकबेथ से कम लेकिन महान होगा, स्वयं राजा नहीं बनेगा लेकिन भविष्य के राजाओं का पिता होगा। जब रॉस और एंगस मैकबेथ को कॉडर का थेन घोषित करने आते हैं, तो भविष्यवाणी का पहला भाग सच हो जाता है। मैकबेथ तुरंत डंकन की हत्या का विचार करने लगता है।
डंकन अपने बेटे मैल्कम को स्कॉटलैंड के उत्तराधिकारी के रूप में घोषित करता है, जो मैकबेथ के रास्ते में एक बाधा बन जाता है। मैकबेथ इनवरनेस में अपने महल में डंकन का स्वागत करने की तैयारी करता है।

लेडी मैकबेथ को अपने पति का पत्र मिलता है जिसमें चुड़ैलों की भविष्यवाणी का वर्णन है। वह तुरंत रानी बनने की संभावना को समझ जाती है, लेकिन डरती है कि उसके पति में "मानवीय दयालुता का दूध बहुत अधिक" है। जब उसे पता चलता है कि डंकन उसी रात आ रहे हैं, तो वह अंधेरी शक्तियों का आह्वान करती है: "मुझे यहाँ अलिंगी बना दो" और पश्चाताप की राह को बंद करने की प्रार्थना करती है। वह मैकबेथ से कहती है कि "निर्दोष फूल की तरह दिखो, लेकिन उसके नीचे सर्प बनो।"
डंकन इनवरनेस पहुंचता है और महल की मधुर हवा की प्रशंसा करता है - एक भयंकर विडंबना, क्योंकि अंदर उसकी हत्या की योजना बनाई जा रही है।

मैकबेथ अकेले में हत्या पर विचार करता है। एक लंबे एकालाप में, वह डंकन की हत्या के खिलाफ सभी कारणों पर विचार करता है - डंकन उसका रिश्तेदार, राजा और मेहमान है। वह स्वीकार करता है कि उसकी एकमात्र प्रेरणा "उछलती महत्वाकांक्षा" है। वह लेडी मैकबेथ से कहता है कि वह आगे नहीं बढ़ेगा। लेकिन लेडी मैकबेथ उसकी मर्दानगी पर सवाल उठाती है, उसे कायर कहती है, और यहाँ तक कहती है कि वह अपने स्तनपान करते शिशु का सिर तोड़ देगी बजाय एक ऐसी प्रतिज्ञा तोड़ने के। वह अपनी हत्या की योजना बताती है - वे चैंबरलेन को नशे में धुत्त करेंगे और उन पर दोष लगाएंगे। मैकबेथ अंततः मान जाता है।
अंक 2: हत्या और उसके तुरंत बाद

आधी रात के बाद, बैंको और उसका बेटा फ्लीन्स महल के आँगन में घूम रहे हैं, नींद नहीं आ रही। बैंको को तीन विचित्र बहनों का सपना आया है। मैकबेथ उनसे मिलता है और झूठ बोलता है कि उसने चुड़ैलों के बारे में नहीं सोचा। अकेले रह जाने पर, मैकबेथ को एक भयानक मतिभ्रम होता है - एक खंजर हवा में तैर रहा है, डंकन के कक्ष की ओर इशारा करता हुआ। अपने प्रसिद्ध "खंजर" एकालाप में, वह पूछता है: "क्या यह वह खंजर है जो मैं अपने सामने देख रहा हूँ?" एक घंटी बजती है - लेडी मैकबेथ का संकेत - और मैकबेथ डंकन के कक्ष की ओर बढ़ता है।

लेडी मैकबेथ तनाव में प्रतीक्षा करती है, चैंबरलेन के पेय में नशीली दवा मिला चुकी है। मैकबेथ खून से सने हाथों के साथ लौटता है: "मैंने काम कर दिया है।" वह तुरंत मनोवैज्ञानिक यातना से ग्रस्त हो जाता है। उसने डंकन के बेटों को "भगवान हमें आशीर्वाद दो" कहते सुना, लेकिन खुद "आमीन" नहीं कह सका। उसने एक आवाज सुनी: "मैकबेथ नींद की हत्या करता है" - भविष्यवाणी करते हुए कि वह "अब और नहीं सोएगा।"

लेडी मैकबेथ उसकी कमजोरी से निराश होती है। जब मैकबेथ खूनी खंजर लेकर आता है जो पहरेदारों के पास होने चाहिए थे, वह उन्हें वापस जाने से इनकार करता है। लेडी मैकबेथ खुद खंजर लेती है और उन्हें पहरेदारों पर रखती है, उन्हें डंकन के खून से सना देती है। दरवाजे पर जोर से दस्तक होती है, और वे भाग जाते हैं।

नशे में धुत्त द्वारपाल अंततः मैकडफ और लेनॉक्स को अंदर आने देता है। मैकडफ डंकन के कक्ष में जाता है और तुरंत हत्या की खोज करता है। वह "भयावहता, भयावहता, भयावहता!" चिल्लाते हुए बाहर आता है और अलार्म बजाता है। जब लेनॉक्स बताता है कि चैंबरलेन के पास खून और बिना पोंछे खंजर पाए गए, तो मैकबेथ घोषणा करता है कि उसने डंकन के प्रति प्रेम के गुस्से में पहरेदारों को मार दिया। लेडी मैकबेथ सुविधाजनक रूप से बेहोश हो जाती है।

मैल्कम और डोनलबेन निजी तौर पर बात करते हैं, यह महसूस करते हुए कि वे खतरे में हैं। वे भागने का फैसला करते हैं - मैल्कम इंग्लैंड और डोनलबेन आयरलैंड। उनका भागना उन्हें संदिग्ध बना देता है, और मैकबेथ को राजा चुना जाता है।
अंक 3: पागल राजा

अब राजा मैकबेथ के दरबार में बैंको को संदेह है कि मैकबेथ ने राजमुकुट के लिए "सबसे बुरी तरह खेला।" मैकबेथ बैंको से उसकी योजनाओं के बारे में पूछता है, यह जानते हुए कि वह और फ्लीन्स शाम को घोड़े पर निकलेंगे। अकेले, मैकबेथ बैंको के प्रति अपने गहरे डर को प्रकट करता है। वह नाराज है कि उसने डंकन की हत्या केवल बैंको के वंशजों को सिंहासन देने के लिए की। मैकबेथ दो हत्यारों को नियुक्त करता है, उन्हें बैंको और फ्लीन्स दोनों को मारने के लिए मना लेता है।

लेडी मैकबेथ, अब रानी, अपनी असंतुष्टि व्यक्त करती है: "कुछ भी नहीं है, सब कुछ खर्च हो गया है, जहाँ हमारी इच्छा संतोष के बिना प्राप्त होती है।" मैकबेथ भी दुखी है। लेडी मैकबेथ उसे सलाह देती है: "जो हो चुका है, वह हो चुका है," लेकिन मैकबेथ कहता है कि साँप केवल "घायल है, मरा नहीं।" वह बैंको के खिलाफ अपनी योजना का संकेत देता है लेकिन विवरण साझा नहीं करता: "प्रिये, ज्ञान से निर्दोष रहो, जब तक तुम कार्य की तारीफ न करो।"
हत्यारे बैंको पर हमला करते हैं। बैंको फ्लीन्स से चिल्लाता है: "हे, विश्वासघात! भागो, अच्छे फ्लीन्स, भागो!" बैंको मारा जाता है, लेकिन फ्लीन्स अंधेरे में भाग निकलता है।

मैकबेथ एक भव्य दावत की मेजबानी करता है। पहला हत्यारा प्रकट होता है और बैंको की मृत्यु की रिपोर्ट करता है लेकिन फ्लीन्स के भागने की भी। मैकबेथ गहराई से परेशान है। जब वह बैठने जाता है, तो उसे अपनी जगह पर बैंको का भूत दिखाई देता है। वह भयभीत होकर भूत को संबोधित करता है: "तुम नहीं कह सकते कि मैंने यह किया। मुझ पर अपने खूनी बाल कभी मत हिलाओ।" लॉर्ड भ्रमित हैं; लेडी मैकबेथ उसके व्यवहार को एक पुरानी बीमारी बताने की कोशिश करती है। भूत फिर से प्रकट होता है, और मैकबेथ फिर से नियंत्रण खो देता है। लेडी मैकबेथ जल्दी से मेहमानों को विदा कर देती है।

अकेले में, मैकबेथ मैकडफ की अनुपस्थिति को संदिग्ध बताता है। वह चुड़ैलों से दोबारा मिलने का संकल्प करता है: "मैं खून में इतना गहरा कदम रख चुका हूँ कि अगर मैं और आगे न बढ़ूं, तो वापस लौटना उतना ही कठिन होगा जितना आगे जाना।"
हेकेट, जादूगरी की देवी, चुड़ैलों को डांटती है। वह मैकबेथ को झूठा आत्मविश्वास देने की योजना बनाती है: "सुरक्षा नश्वर लोगों का सबसे बड़ा दुश्मन है।"

लेनॉक्स और एक स्कॉटिश लॉर्ड भारी विडंबना के साथ हाल की घटनाओं पर चर्चा करते हैं, मैकबेथ के अपराध की ओर इशारा करते हुए। वे बताते हैं कि मैकडफ इंग्लैंड में मैल्कम से मिलने गया है, और राजा एडवर्ड उनके उद्देश्य का समर्थन करेगा।
अंक 4: दूसरी भविष्यवाणी और स्थिति बदलती है

तीन चुड़ैलें एक उबलती कड़ाही के चारों ओर इकट्ठी होती हैं, अपने प्रसिद्ध मंत्र का जाप करती हैं: "दोगुना, दोगुना परिश्रम और संकट; आग जलो, और कड़ाही उबले।" मैकबेथ आता है और उत्तर की मांग करता है। चुड़ैलें तीन भ्रामक दर्शन बुलाती हैं।
पहला दर्शन (एक सशस्त्र सिर): "मैकबेथ! मैकबेथ! मैकबेथ! मैकडफ से सावधान रहो, फाइफ के थेन से सावधान रहो।"
दूसरा दर्शन (एक खूनी बच्चा): "खूनी, साहसी और दृढ़ रहो। मनुष्य की शक्ति का मजाक उड़ाओ, क्योंकि स्त्री से जन्मा कोई भी मैकबेथ को नुकसान नहीं पहुंचा सकता।"
तीसरा दर्शन (एक पेड़ लिए हुए मुकुटधारी बच्चा): "मैकबेथ कभी पराजित नहीं होगा जब तक कि महान बिरनम वुड ऊंची डंसिनेन पहाड़ी की ओर उसके खिलाफ नहीं आता।"

मैकबेथ खुश होता है, मानते हुए कि जंगल नहीं चल सकते और हर कोई स्त्री से जन्मा है। फिर भी वह पूछता है कि क्या बैंको के वंशज राज करेंगे। चुड़ैलें आठ राजाओं का एक जुलूस दिखाती हैं, सभी बैंको से मिलते-जुलते, और बैंको का भूत एक दर्पण लेकर और राजाओं को दिखाता है। मैकबेथ भयभीत है।

लेनॉक्स प्रवेश करता है और बताता है कि मैकडफ इंग्लैंड भाग गया है। मैकबेथ, क्रोधित, तुरंत फैसला करता है: "मैं मैकडफ के महल पर हमला करूंगा, फाइफ को जब्त करूंगा, उसकी पत्नी, उसके बच्चों को तलवार की धार दूंगा।"

फाइफ में मैकडफ के महल में, लेडी मैकडफ अपने पति को छोड़कर जाने के लिए शिकायत करती है। वह अपने युवा बेटे के साथ मार्मिक बातचीत करती है, जो अपनी उम्र से परे बुद्धि दिखाता है। एक दूत आता है और उन्हें तुरंत खतरे की चेतावनी देता है। वह उनसे भागने की विनती करता है, लेकिन बहुत देर हो चुकी है। हत्यारे प्रवेश करते हैं। जब उन्हें बताया जाता है कि मैकडफ एक गद्दार है, तो युवा बेटा बहादुरी से अपने पिता की रक्षा करता है: "तू झूठ बोलता है, तू बाल-उलझे खलनायक!" हत्यारे लड़के को छुरा घोंप देते हैं, जो अपनी मां से भागने के लिए चिल्लाता है। लेडी मैकडफ और उसके सभी बच्चे मार दिए जाते हैं।

इंग्लैंड में, मैल्कम मैकडफ की वफादारी का परीक्षण करता है। वह खुद को मैकबेथ से भी अधिक दुष्ट बताता है - कामुक, लालची, और सभी "राजा-योग्य गुणों" से रहित। जब मैकडफ अंततः टूट जाता है और मैल्कम को "शासन करने योग्य नहीं" घोषित करता है, तो मैल्कम सच्चाई प्रकट करता है - यह सब एक परीक्षण था। उसके पास ये दोष नहीं हैं। वह बताता है कि दस हजार अंग्रेजी सैनिक स्कॉटलैंड पर आक्रमण के लिए तैयार हैं।

रॉस स्कॉटलैंड से आता है। वह हिचकिचाता है, फिर अंततः मैकडफ को बताता है कि उसकी पत्नी, बच्चे और नौकर सभी बेरहमी से मार दिए गए। मैकडफ स्तब्ध है: "क्या मेरे सभी सुंदर बच्चे? क्या तुमने कहा सभी?" मैल्कम उसे दुःख को प्रतिशोध में बदलने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करता है। मैकडफ शपथ लेता है: "मुझे भी इसे एक मनुष्य के रूप में महसूस करना होगा।" वह प्रार्थना करता है कि स्वर्ग मैकबेथ को उसके आमने-सामने लाए।
अंक 5: मैकबेथ का पतन

डंसिनेन में, एक डॉक्टर और एक सज्जन महिला लेडी मैकबेथ के परेशान करने वाले व्यवहार को देखते हैं। वह अपनी आँखें खुली रखकर नींद में चलती है, लगातार एक मोमबत्ती ले जाती है। लेडी मैकबेथ प्रवेश करती है, जुनूनी रूप से अपने हाथ रगड़ती है। वह प्रसिद्ध पंक्ति बोलती है: "बाहर निकलो, शापित धब्बे! बाहर निकलो, मैं कहती हूँ!" वह अनजाने में डंकन की हत्या की रात को फिर से दोहराती है: "फिर भी किसने सोचा होगा कि बूढ़े आदमी में इतना खून होगा?" वह लेडी मैकडफ का उल्लेख करती है और खून की गंध के बारे में जुनूनी हो जाती है: "अरब के सभी इत्र इस छोटे हाथ को मीठा नहीं करेंगे।" डॉक्टर घोषणा करता है: "उसे चिकित्सक से अधिक दिव्य की आवश्यकता है।"

स्कॉटिश रईस अंग्रेजी सेना के साथ जुड़ने के लिए मार्च करते हैं। वे रिपोर्ट करते हैं कि मैकबेथ डंसिनेन कैसल को मजबूत कर रहा है। केथनेस कहता है कि मैकबेथ को लगता है कि उसका खिताब "उस पर ढीला लटक रहा है, जैसे एक बौने चोर पर विशालकाय का वस्त्र।"

डंसिनेन में, मैकबेथ तेजी से पागल होता जा रहा है, लेकिन चुड़ैलों की भविष्यवाणियों पर निर्भर रहता है। वह दोहराता है: "जब तक बिरनम वुड डंसिनेन तक नहीं आता, मैं डर से खराब नहीं हो सकता।" एक नौकर दस हजार अंग्रेजी सैनिकों की खबर लेकर आता है। मैकबेथ अपने कवच के लिए बुलाता है, हालांकि सेटन कहता है कि अभी इसकी आवश्यकता नहीं है। मैकबेथ अपने जीवन की थकान व्यक्त करता है: "मैं काफी लंबा जी चुका हूँ। मेरा जीवन पीली पत्ती में गिर गया है।" वह महसूस करता है कि उसके पास "सम्मान, प्रेम, आज्ञाकारिता, मित्रों के समूह" नहीं हैं - केवल "शाप, गहरे लेकिन जोर से नहीं।"
बिरनम वुड के पास, मैल्कम आदेश देता है कि प्रत्येक सैनिक एक शाखा काटे और उसे अपने सामने ले जाए, उनकी संख्या को छुपाने के लिए। वे आगे बढ़ते हैं, चलता हुआ जंगल डंसिनेन की ओर जाना शुरू करता है।

डंसिनेन के अंदर, मैकबेथ आत्मविश्वास से कहता है कि उसका महल किसी भी घेराबंदी का सामना कर सकता है। महिलाओं की चीख सुनाई देती है। सेटन वापस आता है और रिपोर्ट करता है: "रानी, मेरे प्रभु, मर गई है।" मैकबेथ अपने प्रसिद्ध निराशावादी एकालाप के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है: "कल, और कल, और कल" - जीवन की निरर्थकता के बारे में। वह जीवन को "एक मूर्ख द्वारा बताई गई कहानी, ध्वनि और रोष से भरी, कुछ भी नहीं बताती" के रूप में वर्णित करता है।
एक दूत असंभव खबर लेकर आता है: बिरनम वुड डंसिनेन की ओर बढ़ता दिख रहा है। मैकबेथ अचानक चुड़ैलों के धोखे को समझता है। फिर भी वह लड़ने का संकल्प करता है: "कम से कम हम अपनी पीठ पर हार्नेस लगाकर मरेंगे।"
युद्ध के मैदान में, मैकबेथ यंग सीवार्ड का सामना करता है और आसानी से उसे मार देता है, घोषणा करते हुए: "तू स्त्री से जन्मा था।" मैकडफ मैकबेथ को खोजता है, केवल राजा के साथ व्यक्तिगत प्रतिशोध चाहता है।

अंततः मैकडफ मैकबेथ को ढूंढ लेता है: "मुड़ो, नरक के कुत्ते, मुड़ो!" मैकबेथ स्वीकार करता है: "मेरी आत्मा पहले से ही तुम्हारे खून से बहुत भारी है।" वह अपने आकर्षित जीवन के बारे में घमंड करता है - वह "स्त्री से जन्मे" किसी व्यक्ति द्वारा नहीं मारा जा सकता।

मैकडफ विनाशकारी रहस्योद्घाटन के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है: "मैकडफ अपनी मां के गर्भ से समय से पहले निकाला गया था।" वह सिजेरियन सेक्शन द्वारा पैदा हुआ था, प्राकृतिक जन्म के माध्यम से नहीं। मैकबेथ भयभीत है, चुड़ैलों को कोसता है जिन्होंने उसे दोहरे अर्थों से धोखा दिया। वह समझता है कि "छल करने वाले शैतानों" ने द्विअर्थी शब्दों में बात की - एक अर्थ में सच लेकिन दूसरे में झूठ।

मैकबेथ का आत्मविश्वास पूरी तरह से ढह जाता है। वह शुरू में लड़ने से इनकार करता है, लेकिन जब मैकडफ उसे आत्मसमर्पण करने और एक राक्षस की तरह प्रदर्शित किए जाने की धमकी देता है, तो मैकबेथ की योद्धा भावना वापस आती है। वह घोषणा करता है: "लगा दो, मैकडफ, और शापित हो वह जो पहले चिल्लाए 'रुको, बहुत हो गया!'" वे मंच के बाहर एकल युद्ध में लड़ते हैं।

मैल्कम, सीवार्ड, रॉस और अन्य रईस महल में प्रवेश करते हैं, जिसे पूरी तरह से कब्जा कर लिया गया है। रॉस बताता है कि यंग सीवार्ड बहादुरी से लड़ते हुए मर गया। सीवार्ड पूछता है कि क्या उसके बेटे के घाव सामने थे या पीठ पर। यह जानकर कि उसका बेटा दुश्मन का सामना करते हुए मरा, सीवार्ड एक सैनिक के भाग्य के रूप में मृत्यु को स्वीकार करता है।

मैकडफ एक डंडे पर मैकबेथ का कटा हुआ सिर लेकर प्रवेश करता है। वह मैल्कम का अभिवादन करता है: "जय हो, राजा! क्योंकि तुम वही हो। देखो जहाँ हड़पने वाले का शापित सिर खड़ा है।" वह घोषणा करता है कि स्कॉटलैंड स्वतंत्र है और सभी को मैल्कम के राज्याभिषेक को देखने के लिए आमंत्रित करता है।

राजा के रूप में मैल्कम का पहला भाषण उन लोगों को धन्यवाद देता है जिन्होंने लड़ाई में उसका समर्थन किया। वह घोषणा करता है कि वह नए अर्ल बनाएगा, स्कॉटलैंड के पहले अर्ल अंग्रेजी फैशन में। मैल्कम मैकबेथ के अत्याचार से भागे सभी निर्वासितों को वापस बुलाने का वादा करता है। वह मैकबेथ के क्रूर मंत्रियों और एजेंटों को न्याय के कटघरे में लाने की प्रतिज्ञा करता है।

मैल्कम प्रकट करता है कि लेडी मैकबेथ अपने हाथों से मर गई, उसकी आत्महत्या की पुष्टि करते हुए। वह "माप, समय और स्थान में" स्कॉटलैंड को बहाल करने के लिए सभी आवश्यक कार्य करने का वादा करता है। मैल्कम सभी को स्कोन में अपने राज्याभिषेक के लिए आमंत्रित करता है, जहाँ स्कॉटिश राजाओं को पारंपरिक रूप से ताज पहनाया जाता है।

नाटक व्यवस्था बहाल होने, वैध राजत्व की वापसी, और स्कॉटलैंड के उपचार के वादे के साथ समाप्त होता है। मैल्कम के अंतिम शब्द बहाली और अत्याचारी शासन के अंत पर जोर देते हैं। सभी भविष्यवाणियाँ पूरी हो गई हैं, हालांकि उन तरीकों से जिनकी मैकबेथ ने कभी कल्पना या समझ नहीं की थी।
Who Killed Whom in Macbeth
Macbeth kills:
King Duncan (off-stage, Act 2, Scene 2)
Duncan’s two chamberlains/guards (Act 2, Scene 3)
Young Siward (Act 5, Scene 7)
Macbeth orders the killing of:
Banquo (Act 3, Scene 3)
Lady Macduff and her children (Act 4, Scene 2)
Macduff kills:
Macbeth (Act 5, Scene 8)
Unknown murderers kill:
Macdonwald (killed by Macbeth before the play begins, reported in Act 1, Scene 2)

Major Themes in Macbeth
Ambition: The destructive effects of unchecked ambition
Fate vs. Free Will: The conflict between prophecy and personal choice
Power: The corrupting influence of power and its psychological effects
Guilt and Conscience: The psychological consequences of evil deeds
The Supernatural: The influence of supernatural elements on human affairs
Appearances vs. Reality: The contrast between how things appear and what they truly are
Manhood and Gender Roles: How concepts of masculinity and femininity drive behavior
Loyalty and Betrayal: The consequences of breaking bonds of loyalty
Order vs. Chaos: The disruption of natural order through regicide
Blood: As a symbol of guilt, violence, and the impossibility of cleansing oneself after murder
Literary Devices in Macbeth
Dramatic Irony: Audience knows Duncan’s fate while he praises Macbeth’s loyalty
Soliloquy: Macbeth’s internal struggles revealed through private speeches
Paradox: “Fair is foul, and foul is fair”
Symbolism: Blood symbolizing guilt; darkness and light representing evil and good
Foreshadowing: The witches’ prophecies foreshadow the entire plot
Imagery: Recurring images of blood, darkness, sleep, and animals
Supernatural Elements: Witches, ghosts, and apparitions
Asides: Characters speak directly to audience while other characters cannot hear
Metaphor: “Life’s but a walking shadow, a poor player”
Simile: “My thought, whose murder yet is but fantastical, shakes so my single state of man that function is smothered in surmise, and nothing is but what is not”
Equivocation: Language that has double meanings throughout the play
Key Motifs
Blood: Representing guilt, violence, and honor
Sleep: Representing innocence, peace, and the consequences of guilt
Darkness: Representing evil, death, and concealment
Hallucinations: Representing guilt and psychological breakdown
Animals: Used to characterize people and situations (serpent, owl, falcon)
Children: Representing the future and legacy
Clothing: Representing the false appearance of kingship
Hands: Representing guilt and the inability to wash away sin
Historical Context of Macbeth
Written during the reign of King James I of England (James VI of Scotland)
James I was interested in witchcraft and wrote “Daemonologie” (1597)
The play likely flattered James I by portraying his ancestor Banquo positively
The historical Macbeth ruled Scotland for 17 years (1040-1057), much longer than in the play
The play explores the consequences of regicide at a time when the divine right of kings was a powerful concept
The Gunpowder Plot of 1605 (attempt to assassinate James I) likely influenced Shakespeare
Explores themes of legitimate succession, a concern after Elizabeth I’s death
Significance and Interpretations
Considered one of Shakespeare’s darkest and most powerful tragedies
Often interpreted as a cautionary tale about the corrupting influence of ambition
Psychological study of guilt and its manifestations
Explores questions of fate, free will, and personal responsibility
Examines the nature of evil and whether humans are inherently good or evil
Presents a disruption of natural order that must be restored
Contains some of Shakespeare’s most poetic language and memorable characters
Continues to be one of Shakespeare’s most frequently performed plays

# Chapter 30: A Marriage Proposal
Anton Chekhov Biography
Born: January 29, 1860, in Taganrog, Russia
Died: July 15, 1904, in Badenweiler, Germany (age 44)
Full name: Anton Pavlovich Chekhov
Nationality: Russian
Occupation: Physician, playwright, and short story writer
Education: Moscow University Medical School (graduated 1884)
Literary period: Realism
Major works: “The Cherry Orchard,” “The Seagull,” “Uncle Vanya,” “Three Sisters,” “The Lady with the Dog,” “A Marriage Proposal”
Chekhov began writing to support his family while studying medicine
He continued practicing medicine throughout his literary career
He is considered one of the greatest short story writers in history
He suffered from tuberculosis for much of his adult life
He made a journey to the remote prison island of Sakhalin in 1890 to document conditions there
His writing style is characterized by brevity, precision, and objectivity
He pioneered stream-of-consciousness techniques and the “indirect action” dramatic principle
He was influenced by Leo Tolstoy and influenced writers like James Joyce and Ernest Hemingway
Chekhov’s gun principle: “If in the first act you have hung a pistol on the wall, then in the following one it should be fired”
Play Information
Original title: Предложение (Predlozheniye)
Written: 1888-1889
First published: 1889
First performed: April 1890 at the Abramova Theater in Moscow
Genre: One-act farce/vaudeville comedy
Language: Russian
Setting: Late 19th century rural Russia (Chubukov’s estate)
Performance time: Approximately 25-30 minutes
Original classification: “A joke in one act” by Chekhov himself
Publication: First appeared in the journal “Novoe Vremya” (New Times)
Play structure: Written in continuous action without scene breaks
Translation: First English translation appeared in 1912
Notable productions: Moscow Art Theater production directed by Constantin Stanislavski
Number of Characters
Total characters: 3
Male characters: 2
Female characters: 1
Speaking roles: 3
Non-speaking roles: 0
Offstage characters mentioned: Several servants (never appear)
Character Names and Relations
Stepan Stepanovich Chubukov
Age: Around 60-70 years old
Occupation: Landowner, gentleman farmer
Relation: Father of Natalya
Personality traits: Irascible, proud, easily excitable, concerned with appearances
Physical description: Elderly Russian landowner, traditionally dressed
Background: Widowed, managing his estate with his daughter
Motivation in the play: Wishes to see his daughter married before he dies
Notable quotes: “And it’s a good thing, too. What’s the sense of talking? You were just in the garden arguing about Meadow Oxen, and now you’ve got the Squeezing Tongs on the brain!”
Ivan Vassilevitch Lomov
Age: Around 35 years
Occupation: Landowner, neighboring farmer
Relation: Neighbor and potential suitor to Natalya
Personality traits: Hypochondriac, anxious, easily agitated, formal, nervous
Physical description: Well-dressed gentleman in formal attire (frock coat, gloves)
Background: Wealthy bachelor concerned about his health
Motivation in the play: To propose marriage to Natalya for practical reasons
Medical conditions: Claims to suffer from palpitations, insomnia, and various nervous disorders
Notable quotes: “My heart’s beating awfully… My lips are trembling, and there’s a lump in my throat… No, I must go and have a drink of water first…”
Natalya Stepanovna Chubukov
Age: Around 25 years old
Occupation: Manages household affairs on her father’s estate
Relation: Daughter of Stepan Chubukov
Personality traits: Strong-willed, argumentative, proud, passionate about property
Physical description: Young Russian woman, described as “a young woman of marriageable age”
Background: Single woman managing domestic affairs on her father’s estate
Motivation in the play: Initially unaware of Lomov’s intentions, fiercely defensive of family property
Skills mentioned: Good household manager, knowledgeable about hunting dogs
Notable quotes: “Guess! If you spent the whole day chattering about trifles like a magpie, you wouldn’t have time to go hunting!”
Plot in 10 Bullet Points
Ivan Vassilevitch Lomov, a nervous hypochondriac landowner, arrives at the home of his neighbor Stepan Stepanovich Chubukov, dressed formally in a frock coat.
Lomov reveals to Chubukov that he has come to ask for his daughter Natalya’s hand in marriage, citing practical reasons like their neighboring estates and his advancing age (35).
Chubukov is delighted and goes to call his daughter, but before Lomov can propose, they begin discussing their property boundaries.
An argument erupts between Lomov and Natalya about the ownership of Oxen Meadows, a piece of land that both families claim belongs to them.
The dispute escalates to the point where Lomov begins experiencing heart palpitations and Chubukov returns to find them in a heated debate.
All three characters engage in a fierce argument about the meadows, with Lomov eventually leaving in anger without proposing.
After Lomov leaves, Chubukov reveals to Natalya that Lomov had actually come to propose marriage to her.
Natalya, now realizing what she has lost, becomes hysterical and demands her father bring Lomov back immediately.
Chubukov fetches Lomov, who has nearly collapsed from anxiety, and Natalya attempts to restart the conversation about his original purpose for visiting.

Before Lomov can properly propose, they begin a new argument about whose hunting dog is superior (Squeezer vs. Guess), but Chubukov forces them to accept the engagement despite their continuing argument, ending with Lomov nearly fainting as Chubukov calls for champagne.
Complete Scene-by-Scene Summary
Scene 1: Lomov's Arrival and His Intention
Lomov Enters Chubukov's House
Ivan Vassilevitch Lomov is a 35-year-old landowner who visits his neighbor's house.
He is dressed in formal evening wear, showing he has come for something special and important.
Lomov is a hypochondriac, which means he constantly worries about his health and thinks he is sick.
He suffers from heart palpitations, gets nervous very easily, and often complains about various health problems.
He has lived as a bachelor his whole life and has never been married.
Stepan Stepanovitch Chubukov is his neighbor and the owner of the house.
Chubukov is surprised to see Lomov dressed so formally but welcomes him warmly.
Chubukov's Warm Welcome
Chubukov greets Lomov with great enthusiasm and affection.
He calls Lomov "my darling" and other friendly names, showing he likes him.
Chubukov is curious about why Lomov is wearing evening clothes and asks if he's going to a party.
Lomov nervously explains that he has come only to see Chubukov about an important personal matter.
Chubukov invites Lomov to sit down and make himself comfortable.
He offers Lomov a drink and tries to make him feel at ease.
The atmosphere at this moment is friendly and welcoming.
Lomov's Nervous Behavior
Lomov sits down but appears extremely nervous and uncomfortable.
He starts talking in a rambling, confused way because he is so anxious.
He mentions his health problems and complains about his heart palpitations.
Lomov says his lips tremble and his right eyelid twitches when he gets nervous.
He has trouble sleeping at night and often wakes up suddenly.
Chubukov tries to calm him down and asks what he wants to talk about.
Lomov struggles to get to the main point of his visit.
Lomov Explains His Purpose
Lomov finally reveals that he has come to ask for something important.
He explains that he has known the Chubukov family for a very long time.
His family and Chubukov's family have been neighbors and friends for many years.
Lomov mentions that his late aunt and her husband always respected the Chubukov family.
He talks about how the Lomov family and Chubukov family have always had good relations.
Lomov owns land that borders Chubukov's property, making them close neighbors.
He finally says he has come to ask for the hand of Chubukov's daughter in marriage.
Chubukov's Delighted Response
Chubukov is absolutely thrilled and overjoyed when he hears about the proposal.
He embraces Lomov warmly and calls him "my angel" and "my dear friend."
Chubukov says he has been hoping and waiting for this proposal for a long time.
He immediately gives his blessing and says he agrees to the marriage.
Chubukov is very enthusiastic because Lomov is a good neighbor and landowner.
He seems more interested in the practical benefits of the marriage than romance.
Chubukov says his daughter Natalya Stepanovna will be very happy about this.
Natalya is Called
Chubukov decides to call his daughter to meet with Lomov.
He tells Lomov to wait while he fetches Natalya.
Chubukov is so excited that he can barely contain his happiness.
He says he will send Natalya in right away so Lomov can talk to her.
Before leaving, Chubukov again expresses his joy and approval.
Lomov is left alone in the room, waiting nervously for Natalya to arrive.
He appears extremely anxious about the upcoming conversation.
Scene 2: The First Argument - Oxen Meadows
Natalya Enters the Room
Natalya Stepanovna enters the room to meet Lomov.
She is 25 years old and still unmarried, which was considered old for marriage at that time.
Natalya is surprised to see Lomov dressed in formal evening clothes.
She greets him pleasantly and asks about his health.
Lomov complains about his various health problems as usual.
Natalya asks him why he is dressed so formally.
She doesn't know yet that Lomov has come to propose to her.
Lomov Tries to Lead Up to the Proposal
Lomov begins talking nervously, trying to build up to his proposal.
He mentions how their families have been neighbors for a long time.
He talks about the close relationship between their two properties.
Lomov says he has always had great respect for Natalya and her family.
He is very nervous and keeps getting distracted from his main purpose.
Natalya listens politely but doesn't understand where the conversation is going.
Lomov mentions that he owns land next to hers.
The Topic of Oxen Meadows Comes Up
While talking about their neighboring lands, Lomov mentions a place called Oxen Meadows.
Oxen Meadows is a disputed piece of land that lies between their two properties.
Lomov casually mentions that his Oxen Meadows touch Natalya's birch woods.
Natalya immediately corrects him and says the Oxen Meadows belong to her family.
She insists that Oxen Meadows are not his property but hers.
Lomov is surprised by her claim and says the meadows have always belonged to him.
This innocent mention suddenly turns into a serious disagreement.
The Argument Begins
Natalya firmly states that Oxen Meadows have always belonged to the Chubukov family.
Lomov argues back that the meadows have been his family's property for generations.
Natalya says she has never heard such nonsense in her life.
Lomov insists he can show her documents and deeds that prove his ownership.
Natalya becomes increasingly angry and refuses to believe him.
She says the meadows are about twelve acres and are very valuable to her.
Lomov says he doesn't care about the land itself, but about the principle of justice.
Historical Claims Are Made
Lomov explains the history of the Oxen Meadows ownership.
He says his aunt's grandmother gave the peasants of Natalya's great-grandfather's household free use of the meadows.
This was done in exchange for the peasants making bricks for Lomov's family.
The arrangement was meant to be temporary, for a limited period of time.
The peasants used the meadows for forty years, treating them as their own property.
When the arrangement ended, the meadows should have returned to the Lomov family.
Lomov says everyone in the district knows this is true.
Natalya Disputes the History
Natalya completely disagrees with Lomov's version of the history.
She claims that both her grandfather and great-grandfather considered the meadows their own.
Natalya says the land stretches from the border to the Burnt Marsh.
She insists there has never been any dispute about this until now.
Lomov tells her she is wrong and that documents will prove him right.
Natalya becomes more and more upset as the argument continues.
She says she has always known the meadows belonged to her family.
The Argument Escalates
Both Lomov and Natalya raise their voices and become very emotional.
Natalya accuses Lomov of trying to steal her land.
Lomov says he is not trying to steal anything but only claiming what is rightfully his.
Natalya says she would rather give the meadows to peasants than to Lomov.
Lomov responds that he will give the meadows to peasants himself because they are his.
The conversation becomes more and more heated and aggressive.
Both of them completely forget about the marriage proposal.
Lomov's Health Problems Appear
Due to the stress of arguing, Lomov starts experiencing his health symptoms.
He complains that his heart is pounding very fast.
He says his foot has gone numb and he can barely feel it.
Lomov mentions his shoulder hurts and his temples are throbbing.
Despite his physical discomfort, he continues arguing about the meadows.
Natalya shows no sympathy and continues insisting the land is hers.
The argument has made Lomov very agitated and unwell.
Chubukov Enters and Joins the Argument
Chubukov hears the loud voices and comes into the room.
He asks what all the shouting is about.
Natalya immediately complains to her father about Lomov's claims.
She tells him that Lomov is trying to say Oxen Meadows belong to him.
Chubukov is shocked and angry when he hears this.
He immediately takes his daughter's side in the argument.
Chubukov begins shouting at Lomov as well.
Chubukov Defends His Property
Chubukov angrily declares that the Oxen Meadows belong to the Chubukov family.
He calls Lomov a land-grabber and accuses him of trying to cheat them.
Chubukov says the meadows have been theirs for nearly three hundred years.
He refuses to give up even half an acre of the land.
Lomov tries to show him documents, but Chubukov won't listen.
Chubukov insults Lomov and calls him names.
The situation becomes even more chaotic with all three people arguing.
Lomov Becomes More Ill
The argument with both Natalya and her father makes Lomov even sicker.
He complains that his heart is going to burst.
Lomov says his shoulder has come off and his whole side is paralyzed.
He holds his side and appears to be in genuine pain.
Despite his illness, he continues arguing about the ownership of the meadows.
Natalya and Chubukov show little concern for his health.
They are more interested in defending their claim to the land.
The Argument Reaches Its Peak
All three people are now shouting at each other simultaneously.
Chubukov calls Lomov a swindler and a monster.
Lomov calls Chubukov a dishonest person and worse.
Natalya continues to insist loudly that the meadows belong to her.
Everyone is talking at once, and no one is listening to anyone else.
The noise and chaos in the room are overwhelming.
The marriage proposal has been completely forgotten by this point.
Lomov Leaves in Anger
Unable to bear the argument any longer, Lomov storms out of the house.
He is holding his side in pain and still complaining about his heart.
Lomov shouts insults at Chubukov as he leaves.
He threatens to take the matter to court.
Chubukov shouts back at him not to dare set foot in his house again.
Natalya is also still shouting about the meadows being hers.
Lomov exits in a state of anger, pain, and frustration.
Scene 3: Natalya's Realization and Regret
Chubukov's Revelation
After Lomov leaves, Chubukov is still very angry about the argument.
He continues ranting about how terrible Lomov is.
Chubukov calls Lomov a fool and says he had the nerve to come with a marriage proposal.
When he mentions the words "marriage proposal," Natalya suddenly pays attention.
She asks her father what he means by a marriage proposal.
Chubukov realizes he has accidentally revealed something important.
He tells Natalya that Lomov had come specifically to propose to her.
Natalya's Shock and Distress
Natalya is completely shocked when she learns about the proposal.
She can't believe that Lomov had come to propose and she didn't know.
She realizes that's why he was wearing formal evening clothes.
Natalya becomes very upset and starts crying.
She falls into a chair in despair.
Natalya blames her father for not telling her about the proposal earlier.
She is devastated that she argued with Lomov instead of accepting his proposal.
Natalya Wants Lomov Back
Natalya desperately wants Lomov to come back.
She cries and begs her father to bring Lomov back immediately.
Natalya says she wants to marry Lomov and can't let him go.
She admits that she needs to get married and Lomov is a good match.
At 25 years old, she is worried about remaining unmarried.
Natalya says the Oxen Meadows don't matter anymore.
She just wants her father to call Lomov back quickly.
Chubukov's Confusion
Chubukov is confused by his daughter's sudden change of heart.
Just moments ago, she was arguing fiercely about the land.
Now she is crying and saying she wants to marry Lomov.
Chubukov complains that young women are difficult to understand.
He agrees to call Lomov back even though they just had a terrible fight.
Chubukov goes out to find Lomov and bring him back to the house.
Natalya waits anxiously, crying and worrying that Lomov won't return.
Scene 4: Lomov Returns
Lomov is Brought Back
Chubukov manages to convince Lomov to return to the house.
Lomov comes back, still complaining about his health problems.
He says his heart is pounding and his foot is completely numb.
Natalya sees him and stops crying.
Both Natalya and Lomov are awkward and uncomfortable.
They don't know how to start talking after their terrible argument.
Chubukov tries to help them reconcile.
Apologies and Reconciliation Attempt
Chubukov tells them both to forget about their quarrel.
He encourages them to apologize and make peace with each other.
Natalya tries to be friendly and asks about Lomov's health.
Lomov continues complaining about his various ailments.
There is an uncomfortable silence between them.
They avoid talking about the Oxen Meadows argument.
Chubukov urges them to get to the point of the visit.
Lomov Tries to Propose Again
Lomov nervously tries to bring up the subject of marriage.
He is even more anxious than before after their terrible fight.
Lomov struggles to find the right words.
He mentions that he came for a specific purpose.
Natalya waits expectantly, hoping he will propose.
Lomov talks about how he has always respected her family.
He slowly starts leading up to asking for her hand in marriage.
Scene 5: The Second Argument - The Dogs
The Topic of Dogs Comes Up
While talking nervously, Lomov mentions that he went hunting yesterday.
He talks about his hunting dog named Guess (or Ugadi in some translations).
Lomov says that Guess has gone lame, which worries him.
He paid a high price for the dog - 125 rubles.
Lomov mentions that Guess is a very good hunting dog despite going lame.
Natalya listens and then mentions her own hunting dog.
Her dog is named Squeezer (or Otkatai in some translations).
Natalya Claims Her Dog is Superior
Natalya says that Squeezer is much better than Lomov's dog Guess.
She claims Squeezer is worth much more than what Lomov paid for Guess.
Natalya says her father paid only 85 rubles for Squeezer, and it's a better deal.
She insists that Squeezer is the superior hunting dog in every way.
Lomov disagrees and says Guess is clearly the better dog.
Another argument begins to brew between them.
The marriage proposal is once again forgotten.
The Argument About Dogs Escalates
Lomov argues that Guess is a much finer dog than Squeezer.
He says Guess is a pure-bred, excellent hunting dog.
Natalya insists that Squeezer is younger, faster, and better trained.
Lomov claims that Guess has better breeding and comes from better stock.
Natalya says that Guess is too old and looks like a worn-out horse.
Lomov defends his dog passionately and insults Squeezer.
Both of them become increasingly emotional about their dogs.
Personal Insults Begin
The argument stops being about the dogs and becomes personal.
Natalya accuses Lomov of being jealous of her superior dog.
Lomov says Natalya doesn't know anything about hunting dogs.
Natalya claims Lomov is simply too proud to admit he's wrong.
Lomov says all the hunters in the district know Guess is better.
Natalya challenges this and says everyone knows Squeezer is superior.
They both raise their voices and become very angry.
Technical Details Are Argued
Lomov starts discussing the technical faults he sees in Squeezer.
He says Squeezer is overshot, which means its jaw is deformed.
This is a serious defect in a hunting dog, according to Lomov.
Natalya becomes furious at this criticism of her beloved dog.
She defends Squeezer and says it has no such defect.
Lomov insists he can prove that Squeezer is overshot.
The technical argument continues with both sides presenting evidence.
Chubukov Joins the Second Argument
Once again, Chubukov hears the loud arguing and comes into the room.
He is amazed and frustrated that they are fighting again.
Chubukov asks what the problem is now.
Natalya complains that Lomov insulted her dog Squeezer.
Chubukov immediately takes his daughter's side again.
He begins defending Squeezer and attacking Lomov's dog Guess.
The situation becomes chaotic with all three arguing again.
Chubukov Insults Guess
Chubukov says that Guess is old, ugly, and worthless as a hunting dog.
He claims that Guess couldn't keep up with a real dog like Squeezer.
Chubukov insults Lomov personally for praising such a poor dog.
He says every kennel-man in the district has a better dog than Guess.
Lomov becomes very offended by these insults to his dog.
He tries to defend Guess by listing all its good qualities.
The three-way argument becomes louder and more aggressive.
Lomov's Health Crisis
The stress of the second argument makes Lomov's health even worse.
He complains that his heart is beating wildly.
Lomov says everything has gone dark and he can't see properly.
He staggers and holds onto furniture for support.
His face becomes pale and he appears to be very ill.
Despite his obvious distress, the argument continues.
Natalya and Chubukov are too busy arguing to notice how sick Lomov has become.
The Argument Reaches Chaos Again
All three people are shouting simultaneously about the dogs.
Chubukov and Natalya keep insisting Squeezer is superior.
Lomov keeps defending Guess despite his failing health.
Insults and accusations fly back and forth.
No one is listening to anyone else.
The room is filled with loud, angry voices.
It seems impossible that any resolution can be reached.
Scene 6: The Collapse and Resolution
Lomov Collapses
Lomov suddenly becomes very quiet and stops arguing.
He clutches his chest and appears to be in severe pain.
Lomov staggers and looks like he might fall down.
He makes some weak sounds but can't speak clearly.
His face is very pale and he seems to be losing consciousness.
Lomov collapses into a chair or falls to the floor.
He appears to be dead or dying from a heart attack.
Panic and Concern
Natalya sees Lomov collapse and becomes frightened.
She screams and calls for help.
Chubukov also becomes alarmed and rushes to Lomov.
They check to see if he is breathing and if his heart is beating.
Natalya cries that they have killed him with their arguing.
Chubukov tries to revive Lomov by calling his name.
There is genuine panic and fear that Lomov has died.
Natalya's Regret and Desperation
Natalya becomes hysterical, crying that Lomov is dead.
She blames herself and her father for arguing with him.
Natalya says she wanted to marry him and now he's dead.
She wails that she will never get married now.
Natalya calls Lomov "my darling" and "my beloved," though she was arguing with him moments before.
Her concern seems to be partly about Lomov but also about losing her chance to marry.
She begs her father to do something to save him.
Attempts to Revive Lomov
Chubukov tries various methods to wake Lomov up.
He sprinkles water on Lomov's face.
Chubukov shakes Lomov and calls his name loudly.
They check his pulse and breathing.
Natalya fans Lomov with her handkerchief or anything available.
They discuss whether to call a doctor.
Chubukov considers giving Lomov some liquor to revive him.
Lomov Regains Consciousness
After a few moments, Lomov begins to stir.
His eyes open and he looks around in confusion.
Lomov asks where he is and what happened.
He appears weak and disoriented but is alive.
Natalya is greatly relieved and expresses her joy.
Chubukov is also relieved that Lomov didn't die.
They help Lomov sit up and try to make him comfortable.
Quick Decision to Marry
Now that Lomov is conscious, Chubukov wants to act quickly.
He fears that if they wait, another argument will start.
Chubukov decides to arrange the marriage immediately, right now.
He doesn't give Lomov a chance to formally propose.
Chubukov simply announces that Natalya accepts and they are engaged.
He puts Natalya's hand in Lomov's hand.
Chubukov gives them his blessing as a married couple.

Lomov is confused and asks what is happening.
Chubukov explains that Natalya has agreed to marry him.
Lomov is surprised but happy when he realizes he is now engaged.
Natalya confirms that she agrees to the marriage.
Both seem pleased to be engaged, despite their arguments.
Chubukov celebrates the engagement enthusiastically.
He calls for champagne to celebrate the occasion.
Scene 7: The Final Argument
Brief Moment of Happiness
For a brief moment, everyone is happy about the engagement.
Lomov and Natalya are finally betrothed to each other.
Chubukov congratulates them and himself.
They express affection for each other.
Lomov calls Natalya his "treasure" and "darling."
Natalya responds with similar terms of endearment.

The Old Topics Return
However, the moment of peace doesn't last long.
Someone mentions the Oxen Meadows again.
Lomov still insists the meadows belong to him.
Natalya immediately contradicts him and says they are hers.
The same argument from before starts all over again.
Neither of them has changed their position on the ownership.
They begin arguing even though they are now engaged to be married.
Argument About the Dogs Resumes
The topic of their hunting dogs also comes up again.
Lomov mentions that Guess is superior to Squeezer.
Natalya immediately disagrees and defends Squeezer.
They argue about which dog is better, just like before.
Chubukov joins in, taking his daughter's side again.
The three of them start shouting at each other once more.
It's as if the engagement changed nothing about their behavior.
The Play Ends with Chaos
The play ends with all three characters arguing loudly.
They are shouting about the meadows, the dogs, and various other topics.
Lomov complains about his heart palpitations again.
Natalya and Chubukov continue to contradict everything he says.

Key Themes and Character Analysis
The Theme of Marriage Without Love
The play shows marriage being treated as a business arrangement, not a romantic union.
Lomov wants to marry because he is 35 and thinks it's time to settle down.
He chooses Natalya because she is a good housekeeper and neighbor, not because he loves her.
Natalya wants to marry because at 25 she is getting old by society's standards.
She accepts Lomov because he is a landowner with property, not because of feelings.
Neither character ever expresses genuine love or affection for the other.
Their engagement is based on practical considerations like land, wealth, and social position.
The Theme of Petty Arguments
The play satirizes how people fight over meaningless things.
The Oxen Meadows dispute is about a small piece of land that neither family really needs.
The argument about whose dog is better is completely trivial and silly.
Both arguments show how pride prevents people from being reasonable.
The characters care more about winning arguments than about being happy.
Even after getting engaged, they continue their petty quarrels.
This suggests their married life will be filled with constant bickering.
Lomov's Character
Lomov is a hypochondriac who constantly complains about imaginary illnesses.
He is weak-willed and easily agitated, getting upset over small things.
Lomov is stubborn and refuses to admit he might be wrong about anything.
He is more concerned with property and being right than with relationships.
Despite wanting to propose, he keeps getting distracted by arguments.
Lomov represents the absurdity of the Russian landowning class.
His character is both comical and pathetic throughout the play.
Natalya's Character
Natalya is 25 years old, which was considered quite old for an unmarried woman in that era.
She is argumentative and quick-tempered, like her father.
Natalya is practical and realizes she needs to get married for social and economic reasons.
She cares deeply about property and possessions, shown by her fierce defense of the meadows.
Natalya can switch quickly from anger to affection and back again.
She is vain about her possessions, like her dog Squeezer.
Despite wanting to marry Lomov, she can't stop arguing with him.
Chubukov's Character
Chubukov is a typical Russian landowner, concerned mainly with property and status.
He is hot-tempered and always ready to join an argument.
Chubukov always takes his daughter's side in disputes, right or wrong.
He is eager for his daughter to marry Lomov because it's a good match.
Chubukov is practical and decides to finalize the engagement quickly before more arguments start.
He represents the older generation's attitudes toward marriage and property.
Despite the chaos, he celebrates the engagement enthusiastically.
The Satirical Message
Chekhov uses comedy to criticize the values of the Russian upper class.
The play mocks how property is valued more than human relationships.
It satirizes marriages based on economics rather than love.
The endless arguments show how pride and stubbornness destroy happiness.
The characters' behavior is exaggerated to highlight their foolishness.
The play suggests that such a marriage will be unhappy and full of conflict.
Chekhov wants the audience to laugh at but also recognize these behaviors in society.
The Absurdist Elements
The play has an absurdist quality where the same patterns repeat endlessly.
The characters never learn from their mistakes or change their behavior.
Arguments happen for no good reason and resolve nothing.
The engagement doesn't change the relationship between Lomov and Natalya at all.
The play ends exactly as chaotically as the middle sections, with no growth.
This circularity emphasizes the meaninglessness of their disputes.
The absurdity makes the audience both laugh and feel uncomfortable.
Summary of the Complete Play

This one-act comedy is about a marriage proposal that almost doesn't happen because of constant arguing. Lomov visits his neighbor Chubukov to propose to his daughter Natalya, but before he can ask, they start fighting about who owns the Oxen Meadows. The argument becomes so heated that Lomov leaves in anger. When Natalya learns he came to propose, she desperately wants him back. He returns, but they immediately start arguing again, this time about whose hunting dog is better. Lomov eventually collapses from stress, and while he is unconscious, Chubukov quickly arranges the engagement. Even after becoming engaged, Lomov and Natalya continue arguing about the same topics, showing that their marriage will likely be filled with constant quarrels. The play satirizes loveless marriages based on property and the stubborn pride that prevents happiness.

Major Scenes and Dialogue Highlights
Scene 1: Lomov’s Arrival and Initial Conversation with Chubukov

LOMOV: “I’ve come to see you, honoured Stepan Stepanovich, to trouble you with a request. Not once or twice have I already had the privilege of applying to you for help, and you have always, so to speak… I must ask your pardon, I am getting excited. I shall drink some water, honoured Stepan Stepanovich.”
CHUBUKOV: “What does it all mean? Hurry up and speak out!”
LOMOV: “I shall try. The fact is, I’ve come to ask for the hand of your daughter, Natalya Stepanovna.”
CHUBUKOV: “My darling! Ivan Vassilevitch! Say it again—I didn’t hear it all!”
LOMOV: “I have the honour to ask…”

CHUBUKOV: (Interrupting) “My dear fellow… I’m so glad, and so on… Yes, indeed, and all that sort of thing. (Embraces and kisses LOMOV) I’ve been hoping for it for a long time. It’s been my continual desire. (Sheds a tear) And I’ve always loved you, my angel, as if you were my own son.”
Scene 2: The Oxen Meadows Dispute
LOMOV: “The Oxen Meadows, as you know, are mine.”
NATALYA: “Yours? No, excuse me, they’re ours!”
LOMOV: “No, mine, honoured Natalya Stepanovna.”
NATALYA: “Well, I never! How can they be yours? Do be a good boy and don’t upset yourself. Listen! How can they be yours?”
LOMOV: “I’m speaking of those Oxen Meadows which are wedged in between your birchwoods and the Burnt Marsh.”
NATALYA: “Yes, yes… they’re ours.”
LOMOV: “No, you’re mistaken, honoured Natalya Stepanovna, they’re mine.”
NATALYA: “Just think, Ivan Vassilevitch! How long have they been yours?”
LOMOV: “How long? As long as I can remember.”
NATALYA: “Really, you won’t get me to believe that!”
Scene 3: The Hunting Dogs Argument
NATALYA: “Your Guess is certainly not thoroughbred.”
LOMOV: “Not thoroughbred? He is the best dog in the district!”
NATALYA: “Oh, do be quiet! He’s old and as ugly as a worn-out cab-horse.”

LOMOV: “Excuse me, Natalya Stepanovna, but you’ve forgotten that he’s too much of a thoroughbred to be compared with any worn-out cab-horse. Guess is a dog; as for Squeezer, well—it’s too funny to argue. Squeezer is a dog of the first degree, and Guess is—well, a dog!”
NATALYA: “Don’t get excited. Of course it’s you who’s right, and not Papa, and of course you want to be righter than anybody.”
LOMOV: “I’m not getting excited. I just can’t understand such insensitiveness. Squeezer is simply old!”
Scene 4: The Conclusion and Engagement
NATALYA: “You’re angry because Squeezer is better than your Guess, but you’ll feel better if you admit that Squeezer is worse.”
LOMOV: “I’m ill… My heart’s jumping out of my chest! My shoulder’s come off… There’s something sticking in my side…”
CHUBUKOV: “Your heart’s jumping out? He’s dead! (Pulls LOMOV’S sleeve) Ivan Vassilevitch! Ivan Vassilevitch! What have you done to me? He’s dead! (Falls into an armchair) A doctor!”
NATALYA: “What’s the matter with him? What’s the matter with you?”
LOMOV: “I can’t breathe… Water!”
NATALYA: “He’s dead! (Pulls LOMOV by the sleeve) Ivan Vassilevitch! My dear! My treasure! I was joking! The meadows are yours, yours! Take them! Take them! Take anything of ours you want!”
CHUBUKOV: “Take her! Take everything! Just don’t die!”
LOMOV: “Give me water!”
CHUBUKOV: “We consent! Well? Kiss and be damned to you!”
NATALYA: “He’s alive… Yes, yes, I consent!”
CHUBUKOV: “Kiss each other!”
LOMOV: “Eh? Kiss whom? (They kiss) Very nice, too. Excuse me, what’s it all about? Oh, now I understand… my heart… I see… As for those Oxen Meadows, to be honest…”
